The vendored SKILL.md has no fences and no heading deeper than level 2 (checked with grep), so nothing is wrong today. It matters only if a later vendored update adds fences with # lines.
- Optional (claim 2): the test at plugin.test.ts:~484 demotes with line.startsWith('#') while the build uses /^#{1,4} /. The outputs are identical on the current vendored file and the test asserts the '### Frontend Design' start, so it is independent and not a tautology. It could diverge on a future vendored update.
- Optional (claim 3): roles/worker-operations/dev-server.md now reuses a healthy server only when 'the root names' it. If the root omits it, a worker could start a second server on a held port. The skill has the root check the task list first and name the server, so this is a narrow path, and the worker would report the port collision.
- Optional (claim 4): R-DEVSERVER in requirements.md now says 'restart it when it is down'. The skill covers this in 'Share it' ('you have Worker.operations restart it') and the record in 'Start it' step 3, so behavior and text agree. REQUIREMENT_SECTIONS still maps R-DEVSERVER to the old phrase, so the sync test does not prove the restart clause.
- Optional (claim 5): the stop check is command-match plus the root naming the pid. It does not catch a reused pid running an identical command. The role forbids stopping a server someone else started and requires confirming the port is free.
- Optional (claim 6): the frontmatter description of skills/dev-server/SKILL.md still says 'records its URL and command'. It omits the process id and the started-or-reused flag that the body now requires. The body is what the model follows once loaded.
- Optional (claim 7): R-RV allows live inspection of the shared server. roles/reviewer-visual/captures.md still describes only the TUI and desktop capture rule, but it is scoped to those cases ('For a TUI or desktop GUI'), and the shared interface-inspection text covers web live inspection. No contradiction.
- Not run: no live check that a background job started by a one-shot Worker.operations survives that subagent's end. I could only read the lifecycle text.
